title: Trajectory Evaluation via Rollout-Free World Model for End-to-end Autonomous Driving
claim: Prior evaluators roll out a separate future for every candidate; ours builds one shared memory that all candidates read from.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, top-to-bottom flow, red vs green color coding
description: Two rounded panels side by side. The left panel, in red, is titled 'Candidate-Specific Future Rollout'. A top-down intersection scene feeds three dashed candidate trajectories τ1 to τ3. Below, each trajectory drives its own row of future-state frames (t+1, t+2, ... t+T), ending in a score box (S1 to S3). Red boxes at the bottom read 'Cost Scaling', 'Dense Predict' and 'Recursive Errors'. The right panel, in green, is titled 'Shared Memory Future Sparse Readout'. The same scene feeds a single shared scene-memory grid, and the trajectories are drawn as dotted paths with waypoint circles. Colored spatial queries read sparse cells from the grid and each produces a score. Green boxes at the bottom read 'Rollout Free', 'Shared Memory' and 'Planning Aligned'. The eye goes first to the red-versus-green contrast and then to the many frames on the left versus the single grid on the right.
caption: Two paradigms for future-aware trajectory evaluation. Conventional methods evaluate each candidate by rolling out its future states separately. In contrast, RFWorld constructs a shared scene memory once and lets all candidate trajectories read from it directly for rollout-free scoring.
abstract: Although existing candidate trajectory evaluators have substantially improved end-to-end planning accuracy, their underlying mechanism remains suboptimal. Model-based evaluators typically make scoring future-aware by explicitly predicting candidate-conditioned future states over the planning horizon, which we term rollout. However, rollout incurs high inference cost and accumulates prediction errors. We argue that planning does not require reconstructing a full future scene for each candidate, but only future-relevant information for reliable comparison. We therefore propose RFWorld, a Rollout-Free World model for end-to-end trajectory evaluation. RFWorld constructs a shared scene memory and shapes it into a future-readable representation via lightweight training-time temporal readout with semantic supervision, keeping training overhead low. At inference time, candidate trajectories directly query the shared memory via sparse spatial readout for scoring, reducing computation by roughly the planning horizon times the number of candidate trajectories, while avoiding recursive rollout errors. Experiments on NAVSIM and Bench2Drive show that RFWorld learns a more planning-aligned world representation and achieves state-of-the-art performance.
